items.title: ₹10,000 a month for 10 years in flexi cap funds
items.text: A ₹10,000 monthly SIP started in November 2016 in the middle-ranked of the 19 flexi cap funds with a 10-year record (Regular plans) is worth about ₹24.3 lakh today, on ₹12.0 lakh put in: about 14% a year. That decade included the 2020 crash. The weakest fund's SIP is at ₹21.2 lakh and the strongest at ₹32.4 lakh.

items.title: Held for 3 years, large cap funds made money 98% of the time
items.text: Across 21 large cap funds with 10 or more years of history (Regular plans), the middle fund ended 98% of all its 3-year holding periods with a gain, and 82% with more than 7% a year, roughly a fixed-deposit rate. That counts every weekly start date back to 2006, through the 2008 and 2020 crashes. Its worst 3-year stretch was -4.6% a year.

items.title: Flexi Cap: SIPs started at the Nov 2025 high are back in profit
items.text: In 41 of 41 flexi cap funds (Regular plans), a monthly SIP started in November 2025, when the Nifty 50 last peaked, is already worth more than the money put in, although the Nifty 50 itself is still below that high. The median SIP is +7.6%. Instalments made while prices were lower bought more units, which is how an SIP recovers before the market does.

items.title: Where active funds beat their index
items.text: Over the last 3 years, 17 of 23 multi cap funds (Regular plans) beat their index (TRI), the highest share among the main categories. It varies a lot: in elss it was 17 of 37, so which fund you hold matters as much as which category.
